headline: This guy's testosterone
punch: At 28 his growth plates were still wide open.

headline: Everyone credits
body: It's the hormone people tie to male puberty, male bone, male height. So they assume it's also what ends your growth.

headline: The patient
body: A 28 year old man had a mutation that broke his estrogen receptor. His testosterone was normal, slightly high even. Fully masculinised. Everything androgen driven worked exactly like it should.
punch: His epiphyses never fused and he kept growing into adulthood.

headline: And here's the control
body: They gave him estrogen for six months. His free estradiol went up about tenfold. Nothing happened, because the receptor meant to read that signal was broken.
punch: Hormone present. Receiver broken. Plates stayed open.

headline: Which means
body: Aromatase converts androgens into estrogen, including inside growth plate cartilage itself. Testosterone doesn't close your plates directly. It becomes the thing that does.
punch: Cartilage makes its own estrogen on site.

headline: And it works in reverse
body: Block aromatase with letrozole or anastrozole in boys and bone maturation slows down and adult height goes up. Same idea tested forwards, in humans.
punch: Block the conversion, delay the closure.

headline: But don't oversimplify it
body: Block the estrogen receptor completely with fulvestrant in mice, so aromatisation is irrelevant, and testosterone still speeds up skeletal maturation.
punch: Something androgen driven is happening that estrogen can't explain.

headline: There's also a third
body: GPER-1 does roughly the opposite of ER-alpha. It promotes chondrocyte proliferation and delays hypertrophy. It peaks early in puberty then drops as classical estrogen signalling rises.
punch: Estrogen may flip from pro growth to pro closure as puberty runs.

headline: So the honest version
body: Estrogen is the dominant lever on growth plate closure. Human genetics and clinical trials both settle that. Whether androgens also act directly is still genuinely argued over.
punch: Anyone giving you one clean sentence is skipping the argument.
